derivation of ‘comet’ is from Gk κομήτὴς, ‘long-haired’. Comets are traditionally portents of violent
change; cp. II iv 139 and note, IV 317 and note. Rognoni suggests cp. with the decriptions of ominous
portents in Julius Caesar I iii 3–28, II ii 13–24, and Virgil’s Georgics i 466–88, iii 478–566.

from with to by in 1820 was presumably made by S. to the fair copy, but he omitted to complete the
alteration to Nbk 7.
